**Test image observations:**
- Mango leaf showing small, dark, raised/blister-like spots scattered on the surface, especially along the leaf margin
- Spots are round, dark brown to black, and appear to protrude slightly from the leaf surface
- Leaf is otherwise green with no white powdery coating, no black superficial encrustation, no curling/browning

**Matching against classes:**
- **Gall Midge**: "round, blister-shaped galls (~2–3mm diameter) on mango leaves, visible on both sides, can be green/yellow/red/brown to brown-black depending on age" — closely matches the round, dark raised spots
- **Bacterial Canker**: raised black spots but should be angular with chlorotic halos and greasy margins — not observed
- **Sooty Mould**: superficial black encrustation covering broad leaf area — not matching (Sooty Mould reference shows diffuse coating, not discrete small galls)
- Others (Powdery Mildew, Die Back, Cutting Weevil, Anthracnose) — clearly don't match

The small, discrete, round, raised dark spots scattered on the leaf surface are characteristic of Gall Midge galls at a mature (brown-black) stage.

The spots are distinct and not angular (ruling out Bacterial Canker), not a diffuse coating (ruling out Sooty Mould), and not white (ruling out Powdery Mildew)."}
